\chapter{Kikuchi LDC — Main Theorem}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.KikuchiLDC.LDC.MainTheorem
\section{Overview}

This module states the two final lower bounds of the
Alrabiah--Guruswami--Kothari--Manohar development: the main near-cubic bound for
$3$-query locally decodable codes, $k^3 \le n \cdot O(\log^6 n / (\varepsilon^{16}
\delta^{16}))$, equivalently $n = \Omega(k^3 / \mathrm{polylog}\,k)$ for constant
$\delta, \varepsilon$; and the corresponding bound $k \le n^{1 - 2/q} \cdot O(\log n /
(\varepsilon^4 \delta^2))$ for $q$-query codes with $q$ even, obtained from the Kikuchi
matrix for even arity.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Cubic lower-bound inequality for 3-query locally decodable codes]
\lean{main_theorem_ldc_lower_bound}
\label{main_theorem_ldc_lower_bound}
\leanok
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p001-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p005-b008,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p006-b006
}
\uses{NormalLDC}
\difficulty{3}
Let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2$ be integers, and let $\delta, \varepsilon \in (0,1]$.
Suppose $L$ is a normal form $(3,\delta,\varepsilon)$-decodable code with message length
$k$ and block length $n$, whose density parameter equals $\delta$ and whose advantage
parameter equals $\varepsilon$. Then there exists a real constant $C > 0$ for which
\[
  k^3 \;\le\; \frac{n \, C \, (\log n)^6}{\varepsilon^{16}\,\delta^{16}} .
\]
Here $C$ is quantified after $k$, $n$, $\delta$, $\varepsilon$ and the code $L$ have
been fixed, so it is permitted to depend on all of them.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[A constant bound on $k$ of order $n^{1-2/q}\log n$]
\lean{even_q_ldc_lower_bound}
\label{even_q_ldc_lower_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
\statementsource{arXiv.2308.15403}{
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b005,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p010-b009,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b001,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b003,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b005,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b006,
  pdf-b372a20892ce-p011-b007
}
Let $q$ be an even integer with $q \ge 2$, let $k \ge 1$ and $n \ge 2$ be integers, and
let $\delta, \varepsilon > 0$. Then there exists a constant $C > 0$ such that
\[
  k \;\le\; n^{\,1 - 2/q}\cdot\frac{C \,\log n}{\varepsilon^{4}\,\delta^{2}}.
\]
\end{theorem}
